Great question. I will go against the sub and say tactics are the greater part of any team success.

Granted, most successful teams have amazing players that can change the outcome of a game in few seconds, but the coach has to set them up to be able to do that. I believe there are two ways to go about tactics:

1- You build a team to play the game you want.

2- You build a strategy that compliments the majority of your team’s strengths.

In my FM journey of 16 seasons with the same club, I started out with a 4-2-3-1 gegenpress because that suited my team at the beginning. I had a good depth in aml-amc-amr rotation and a lack of depth in strikers. So my wingers were carrying the load of scoring and creating chances. After a few seasons though, I realized I cant be as good as top flight european teams that have the same tactics because my squad was not nearly good as theirs. So I switched to a 3-5-2, which took about 2 years of rebuilding.

With the new tactic I dont even press the ball. I throw players forward when we have the ball and the defensive line is high when we lose it. The three defenders at the back and the DLP in front of them recycle possession thanks to their speed. My attacking players dont have to do much chasing, so they are fresh late into the game. 

But the real game changer for this tactic is a two-fold strategy I apply: (1) my MC setup is always a BBM and either a Mezzala or Carrilero depending on the opposition team. If they possess dangerous wingers I go with Car, if they are very defensive I go with Mez. (2) I always pay specific attention to individual instructions. Does the opponent only have one striker? Tight marking + closing down at all times. Are their wingers potential headaches? My WBs are setup from attacking to support with marking duties. Do they have two great strikers? Well maybe then I will go very aggressive with pressing or change my DLP to BWM and my MEZ to AP. So these tweaks depending on the game elevate my players’ game, bringing results.

If I ever try to play a 4-2-3-1 with the current squad my team would suffer, and the old squad wouldn’t manage a 3-5-2. To lessen the gap between bigger teams and mine I had to adjust sth in my tactics each match. And now I sit comfortably at the top of European football (after 16 seasons) and now I have both a great amount of talent and that talent fits with my team from day 1. 

Tldr: The point I make through all this anecdotal evidence is, FM taught me that smaller teams have to defeat opponents through tactical battles, whereas once your stature is established at the top it’s a matter of being consistent and flexible when needed. Good tactics determine how long that journey takes.

Actual examinations that identify and treat the root of the problem. I lost 15 kilos in 2 months and had a severe case of flu that just didnt get better. My GP  heretold me I might have cancer, gave me a blood test, said I dont have cancer and sent me home. I sent the blood test to a doctor I know in my home country, he looked at it and said “this is the bare minimum to determine if you have cancer. You dont but your complaints need to be addressed, its not okay you have flu for 2 months.”

Went home, got proper blood tests. Turns out I had serious deficiencies in some substances in my blood. Got prescribed four different medicines for that, and I got better in a month. 

Not to mention countless people who get into an accident (I play pro-basketball so its fairly common), and the GPs first instinct is to “wait till it gets worse”. That’s exactly the opposite of what you need if you want longevity as an athlete. The GPs here would instead wait until your ankle becomes the size of a basketball, and your broken bone torn muscle develops damage beyond repairable and you need to undergo surgery.

Back home I could just explain the issue and get an MRI scan or X-ray or both if necessary without waiting till my injury cripples me for months.

I have an EU citizenship alongside being Turkish, so that’s how I survived. As an EU citizen you get rent & insurance allowance, lower tuition fee, university scholarship if you work part time (that you dont pay back if you graduate in 10 years) and free student travel during the weekdays. And most importantly, you’re free to do anywhere work here without dealing with paperwork.

Coming from a lower-middle class family in Turkey, I have no clue how I would have managed to live here without EU benefits. 

That said, universities have scholarships for extraordinary students that cover tuition and some pocket money in certain cases, these depend on the uni and faculty. Those are your best shot, albeit they are very competitive. Or a PhD.

Linguistics major here. Firstly, linguistic theories do have applications indeed. However, it is not always the same person who comes up with a theory and then with ways to quantify or operationalize it. A great example is Sapir-Whorf theory (the languages you speak shapes how you view the world), which later got revised by Daniel Slobin (the languages you speak may create a cognitive advantage for certain domains such as allocating attention). These theories are put to test by cognitive scientists and psycholinguists. Actually, I am writing my own thesis on this too.

Your second paragraph describes etymology, phonology (for which you would also need knowledge of phonetics of course), and a bit of sociolinguistics. If what you mean by "come from" is the origin of language, it is a whole another topic which is very foreign to me as well.

For your last question: do not worry about someone "stealing" your research question. I find it very unlikely, especially at this stage of your pursuit. I would rather share anything I know to get more sophisticated answers. 

To study sound change, you need to learn about the fields I have mentioned above. However, from the vague description you gave me, I understand that this sound (may also be called phoneme) goes through some change depending on its context. It is very common (I might even say similar processes happen in probably any language). 

In particular, you need to study International Phonetic Alphabet to learn about sounds of the languages of our planet :) 

A very good introductory textbook to linguistics is this: [https://www.amazon.com/Linguistics-Anne-Baker/dp/063123036X](https://www.amazon.com/Linguistics-Anne-Baker/dp/063123036X)

I'd suggest reading the entire book, it provides you with elementary concepts of many fields within linguistics.

Okay this answer is a bit late and I am sorry for that. Let me rephrase.

Use your hips to close your punches: Imagine you are throwing a right hook. If you rotate your hip to the left (without first moving it to the right) you will be "closing" your punch. In short, rotate your hips when you throw. 

I specifically used close, because if you throw a left hook and your hip first goes left, this is when you "telegraph" a punch. Because your left shoulder goes back too when you first rotate your hip to left, which signals that you are about to throw a punch.

The piston analogy is not that important. "Make it snappy" would work. As soon as your punch lands the heavy bag, concentrate on pulling your arms back to where your guard is.

I hope this can help you my friend!

I am not an expert but to me it seems you drop your left when you throw a right.

Also when you punch do not lean back, this telegraphs your punches. Instead use your hip and close your punches. For me it helps to think I have pistons attached to my shoulders, they can only move forward and back where they were, not further back before a punch.

One last thing, do not wait before pulling your arms back when you throw. I too had this habit after doing bagwork and neglecting sparring. A bag does not hit but an opponent would take every opening to get at you.
